title: SALT
subtitle: The Empire's Smallest Fear

hero.lede: Not a slideshow with narration. A 40-line sourced film built from 81 procedural plates, eight chapters and a host track that may only repeat what the record already says.

hero.caption: The Empire's Smallest Fear
hero.title: SALT
hero.intro: In 1930 the Raj taxed the one thing every Indian could gather for free. One man picked up a handful of salt, and the Empire discovered a weapon it could not arrest.
hero.description: The production dossier for SALT: 40 sourced lines, 81 procedural plates, eight chapters and a host track that may only restate the record. Every frame assembled on free CI.

intro: A film about 1930, built from a tax act, a handful of salt, a march, a gate and a pact. No stock footage. No paid APIs. Every frame is assembled on free GitHub Actions hardware.
cutBody: The first plate map could not place a single shot. The rebuilt map gives every narration line two plates from two different sets, with eight authored chapters and a cut roughly every three seconds. The storyboard below is the same file the render validates.
closingNote: The first plate map was rejected. The 1080 master is the one that has to earn the release.

stats.note: two shots per line, eight chapters

pipeline.title: Source lock
pipeline.body: The topic is rejected unless it has a human stake, a concrete noun, a turn and a reason to tell it now. Every narration line is tied to a source id before a plate is designed.

pipeline.title: Storyboard
pipeline.body: Forty lines become forty scenes. Each line gets two shots from two different sets, an authored chapter, a camera move and a transition with a reason.

pipeline.title: Procedural sets
pipeline.body: Blender builds the salt crust, the village, the Dharasana gate, the office, the archive and the evidence tables. Each plate carries its own seed, framing and tone.

pipeline.title: Camera and type
pipeline.body: Chromium drives the timeline frame by frame: push-ins, pans, hard cuts, the series card, captions and the lower-third host strip. The camera is code, so every frame is repeatable.

pipeline.title: Score and master
pipeline.body: ffmpeg synthesises the bed, mixes the narration and host voices, burns the SRT into the master and encodes the MP4. Hard cuts carry silence, not a click.

pipeline.title: Free CI
pipeline.body: The render runs on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu CPU. No GPU. No paid runner. The owner's machine writes the code; it does not render the film.

iterations.title: The plate map failed before a frame was rendered
iterations.body: The first final dispatch stopped with FAIL No Blender scene mapped for plate object-01 in salt-march. The fix was not a fallback: all 81 plates were mapped to a semantically matching set, with a per-plate Blender script.

iterations.title: The draft exposed invented host lines
iterations.body: The first host track claimed a court stood for the tax and that the Salt Act was written for them. Neither fact is in the narration, so both were removed. The rebuilt track has 33 lines: sourced restatements, attitudes and bickering, with no duplicate button.

iterations.title: A blurred plate was replaced
iterations.body: One march plate focused on an empty point at the camera, so the whole frame rendered as a smear. The camera now focuses on the march itself, and the plate opens on a readable line of figures.

iterations.title: The master was gated, then released
iterations.body: The 720p draft passed independent QC before the 1080p master was attempted. The final cut keeps the 40 sourced lines, the 33 host lines and the hard-cut grammar, and ships with a 720p site preview.

rules: No paid APIs. Piper, Blender, Chromium and ffmpeg run on free CI.
Every narration line carries a source id; a missing source fails the render.
Hosts may only restate a sourced fact, express an attitude, or bicker. They may not invent a fact.
No actor likeness, no stock footage, no external photo, mesh or texture.
The dead stay off screen. The film shows the record, not the bodies.
A hard cut carries silence. No recurring click between narration lines.
